story: The North Pacific Fishery Management Council's October 9th motion on NMFS's Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan for observers and electronic monitoring, and the machine learning work on EM video

claims.claim: In a motion dated October 9th, the North Pacific Fishery Management Council said it supports the draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan for partial coverage fisheries.
claims.verbatim: Council Motion October 9, 2026 2027 Annual Deployment Plan (ADP) Regulations requiring 100% and 200% observer coverage requirements are unchanged. The Council supports the draft 2027 ADP for partial coverage fisheries.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion page 1, lines 1 to 6. In window. eAgenda lists C1 MOTION uploaded 10/09/2026 09:50 AM. The ADP itself says the Council does not formally approve or disapprove the plan, so write 'supports' or 'backed', never 'approved'.

claims.claim: The Council motion says observer coverage rates and the final budget are expected in the final 2027 ADP in December.
claims.verbatim: Observer coverage rates resulting from the selected design and the final budget are expected in the final ADP in December 2026.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion lines 6 to 7. This is a forward-looking statement, so soften to 'are expected in December'. Corroborated by ADP Executive Summary and slide 9.

claims.claim: The Council motion says regulations requiring 100% and 200% observer coverage are unchanged.
claims.verbatim: Regulations requiring 100% and 200% observer coverage requirements are unchanged.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion line 5.

claims.claim: The Council supports removing vessels from the fixed gear EM pool in 2027 if they have not complied with requirements to update and submit EM Vessel Monitoring Plans for the past 3 years.
claims.verbatim: Removing vessels from the fixed gear electronic monitoring (EM) pool in 2027 who have not complied with requirements to update and submit EM Vessel Monitoring Plans for the past 3 years.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion lines 9 to 11. Same wording as the PCFMAC recommendation.

claims.claim: NMFS identified 32 fixed-gear EM vessels that had not submitted a Vessel Monitoring Plan in 2024, 2025 or 2026, and said they will be placed in the observer pool for the 2027 fishing year.
claims.verbatim: 32 fixed-gear EM vessels were identified as having not submitted a VMP in the past 3 years (2024, 2025, nor 2026). These vessels will be notified of their removal from the fixed-gear EM pool and placement in the observer pool for the 2027 fishing year.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 28. In window (eAgenda upload 10/07/2026). Single-sourced, and the source is the agency's own presentation. The 32 figure does not appear in the ADP document or the motion.

claims.claim: The Council supports a yearly NMFS evaluation that moves fixed gear EM vessels averaging fewer than 3 trips a year over the prior 3 years into the at-sea observer pool and returns their EM equipment for use on active vessels.
claims.verbatim: A yearly evaluation by NMFS to remove vessels from the fixed gear EM pool if they average <3 trips per year over the prior 3 years. These vessels will be placed in the at-sea observer pool and return their EM equipment to be used on active vessels.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion lines 12 to 14. The motion itself names no start year. The start year is in C07.

claims.claim: The draft 2027 ADP says the minimum fishing effort requirements to stay in the fixed-gear EM pool take effect starting in 2028.
claims.verbatim: Additionally, minimum fishing effort requirements to remain in the EM Fixed-gear pool go into effect starting in 2028 (Appendix C).
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Executive Summary p.6 and section 4 p.10. Background. The document is dated September 2026 and posted 09/09/2026, then presented at the October meeting. Corroborated by slide 29 ('Yearly evaluation, beginning during the 2028 ADP') and the PCFMAC report ('Beginning with the 2028 ADP').

claims.claim: Under the draft ADP, vessels with at least 3 years in the fixed-gear EM pool must complete at least 9 trips over the most recent three years to remain in it in 2028.
claims.verbatim: Vessels with at least three (3) years of membership in the EM Fixed-gear pool must complete at least nine (9) trips in the EM Fixed-gear pool over the most recent three year period (i.e., three trips per year on average)
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP p.10. Background document. Slide 29 says the same thing ('< 9 trips total over the prior 3 years').

claims.claim: Under the Council motion, vessels asking to rejoin the fixed gear EM pool need at least 5 trips a year over the prior 3 years.
claims.verbatim: Vessels requesting to rejoin the fixed gear EM pool need at least 5 trips per year over the prior 3 years
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion lines 15 to 16. The ADP gives the 2027 re-entry figure as '15 trips in the last 3 years', which is consistent.

claims.claim: The Council asked NMFS to consider active vessels proposed for removal from the fixed gear EM pool, with more than 0 and fewer than 3 trips, if they can prove they lack bunk space for an observer.
claims.value: more than 0 and fewer than 3 trips
claims.verbatim: The Council requests NMFS provide consideration for active vessels that are proposed to be removed from the fixed gear EM pool (>0 - <3 trips) if they can prove they do not have bunk space for an observer
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion lines 18 to 20. The PCFMAC asked for a 'waiver process'. The Council's wording is softer ('provide consideration'), so do not call it a waiver.

claims.claim: The Council asked NMFS to continue exploring criteria for vessels joining the fixed gear EM pool for the first time.
claims.verbatim: The Council requests NMFS continue to explore criteria for vessels joining for the first time
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion line 17. Context for the deck: the PCFMAC said there should be no obstacles for first-time joiners, but the draft ADP requires 15 trips for new entrants in 2027 (C12). The motion leaves this question open.

claims.claim: The draft ADP says new vessels seeking entry to the fixed-gear EM pool for 2027 must have completed at least 15 trips in the prior three years.
claims.verbatim: New vessels requesting entry into the EM Fixed-gear pool must have completed at least 15 trips in the prior three year period (i.e., five (5) trips per year on average with at least 1 trip per year)
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP p.10. Background. This is a draft provision, and the Council asked NMFS to keep exploring first-time criteria (C11). The PCFMAC report says there should be 'no obstacles (such as prior trip history)' for first-time joiners. Soften to 'the draft plan proposes'.

claims.claim: The Council recognized NMFS's conclusion that moving low-trip fixed gear vessels to the zero selection pool produced no cost efficiency or monitoring gains.
claims.value: no cost efficiency or monitoring gains
claims.verbatim: The Council appreciates the analysis of moving additional fixed gear vessels with few annual trips to the zero selection pool (i.e., no observer coverage requirements) and recognizes the conclusion there were no cost efficiency or monitoring gains identified.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, C1 Motion
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, motion lines 21 to 23. ADP Appendix D says the same: NMFS does not recommend changes to the no-selection pool at this time.

claims.claim: NMFS analyzed 172 fixed-gear EM vessels that had a full three-year fishing history for 2023 through 2025.
claims.verbatim: 2023–2025 Fishing Effort: ● 172 vessels with a full 3-year history
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 25. ADP Appendix C corroborates this: 'Of the 182 vessels in the fixed-gear EM pool over that period, 172 were in the pool for all three years.'

claims.claim: Of those 172 vessels, 39 took no trips over 2023 through 2025 and 133 were active.
claims.verbatim: 39 vessels took no trips, 133 active vessels
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 25. The sum checks (39 + 133 = 172). ADP Appendix C corroborates both figures.

claims.claim: NMFS found that 37 active fixed-gear EM vessels fishing fewer than 3 trips a year were generally not cost-effective.
claims.verbatim: Vessels that fished fewer than 3 trips per year were generally cost-ineffective ○ 37 vessels
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 26. ADP Appendix C adds that these 37 vessels averaged a total of only 60 trips per year. It also says a vessel-by-vessel test found 35 cost-inefficient vessels (over $110K savings) before NMFS chose the simpler trips-per-year rule. Keep 'generally'.

claims.claim: NMFS calculated that applying the under-3-trips threshold moves 39 inactive and 37 active vessels, 76 vessels and 77 trips in all, from fixed-gear EM to observers.
claims.verbatim: Moves 39 inactive and 37 active vessels (< 3 trips per year ) to OB (76 vessels, 77 trips)
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 27, which says this is the threshold 'applied to 2026 fishing effort'. ADP Table C-2 corroborates the 77-trip shift (OB +77, EM -77). This is a modeled scenario, so soften to 'would move'.

claims.claim: NMFS put the total cost difference from applying the under-3-trips threshold at $96,000.
claims.verbatim: Total difference in cost of $96,000 (Table C-1)
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 26. ADP Table C-1 shows savings of $0.096M, the maximum of the thresholds tested. It is an estimate using simplified costs that exclude program management and overhead. Soften to 'an estimated $96,000'. Slide 27 says '~$96K' was reallocated, not saved outright.

claims.claim: In the NMFS scenario, observer cost per trip falls from $10,964 to $9,967, a 9.1% drop.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 27, At-sea Observers row. ADP Table C-3 corroborates it (10,964 to 9,967, -977, -9.1). The arithmetic checks (977/10,964 = 8.9%, which the documents report as 9.1%, a small rounding inconsistency in NMFS's own table). Quote 9.1% as NMFS reports it, as a modeled scenario.

claims.claim: In the same scenario, fixed-gear EM cost per trip falls from $7,494 to $7,017, a 6.4% drop.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 27, Fixed-gear EM row. ADP Table C-3 corroborates it (7,494 to 7,017, -477, -6.4). The arithmetic checks (477/7,494 = 6.4%). This is a modeled scenario.

claims.claim: In the same scenario, the at-sea observer sample rate rises from 12.60% to 13.43%.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 ADP, Table C-2
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Table C-2 p.43. DISCREPANCY: slide 27 prints '12.60% 13.46% +0.83%', but 12.60 + 0.83 = 13.43, which matches the ADP table. Use 13.43% and do not use the slide's 13.46%. Modeled scenario.

claims.claim: In the same scenario, the fixed-gear EM sample rate rises from 16.96% to 19.49%.
claims.verbatim: Fixed-gear EM Sample rate 16.96% 19.49% +2.53%
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 27. ADP Table C-2 corroborates it (EM FIXED summary 16.96 to 19.49, +2.53). The arithmetic checks. This is a modeled scenario.

claims.claim: NMFS told the Council that fixed-gear EM vessels that do not fish enough trips to overcome equipment-related costs are less cost-efficient.
claims.verbatim: Vessels that do not fish enough trips to overcome the equipment-related costs are less cost-efficient
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 25. The same slide says EM vessels 'require equipment maintenance and system replacements', calls this a high 'buy-in' cost (curly quotes in source), and says EM review has 'Low additional costs per selected trip'.

claims.claim: NMFS estimated fixed-gear EM equipment maintenance and annualized system replacement at $6,003 per vessel per year.
claims.verbatim: Equipment maintenance and annualized system replacement costs per vessel ($6,003 per vessel per year for 123 active vessels)
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 17. ADP Appendix B corroborates the figure: 'the recurring annual equipment cost per vessel was estimated at $6,002.96'. Do NOT use the slide's '123 active vessels'. Appendix C counts 133 active vessels over 2023 to 2025, while Appendix B's budget denominator is vessels active in the previous 12 months. The 123 figure appears nowhere else and can't be reconciled from the documents.

claims.claim: NMFS put 2025 at-sea observer costs at $2,937,000 for 1,299 observer days, or $2,260.97 per day.
claims.verbatim: The cost-per-trip was calculated from the 2025 Annual Report (AFSC and AKR 2026) as $2,937,000 for 1,299 observer days, or $2,260.97 per day.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Appendix C p.40. The arithmetic checks (2,937,000 / 1,299 = 2,260.97). The figure includes labor and travel costs. Background (2025 data).

claims.claim: NMFS set a preliminary budget of $5.45 million for 2027 monitoring of the partial coverage fisheries.
claims.verbatim: For this analysis, NMFS set a preliminary budget of $5.45M to support 2027 monitoring of the partial coverage fisheries.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 9. Corroborated by the ADP Executive Summary and the PCFMAC report. The budget is preliminary and will be updated for the final ADP in December, so say 'preliminary'.

claims.claim: The draft ADP describes the 2027 budget as a 14.7% increase from the $4.75 million set in the 2026 ADP.
claims.verbatim: Note that the overall budget is a 14.7% increase from the $4.75M monitoring budget set in the 2026 ADP.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Appendix B Results p.34. The arithmetic checks (5.45 / 4.75 = 1.147). The $4.75M 2026 budget is independently confirmed by IB 26-02 ('The 2026 budget for EM and observer deployment in the partial coverage fisheries is $4.75M.'). Preliminary.

claims.claim: The draft ADP allocates $3,227,000 of the preliminary 2027 partial coverage budget to at-sea observers.
claims.verbatim: At-sea Observer $3,227,000
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 ADP, Table B-1
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Table B-1 p.34. Slide 19 corroborates it. Preliminary allocation.

claims.claim: The draft ADP allocates $1,479,000 of the preliminary 2027 partial coverage budget to fixed-gear EM.
claims.verbatim: EM Fixed-gear $1,479,000
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 ADP, Table B-1
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Table B-1 p.34. Slide 19 corroborates it. Preliminary allocation.

claims.claim: The draft ADP allocates $732,000 of the preliminary 2027 partial coverage budget to trawl EM in the Gulf of Alaska.
claims.verbatim: EM Trawl GOA $732,000
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 ADP, Table B-1
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Table B-1 p.34. Slides 16 and 19 corroborate it. Slide 16 says this excludes trawl EM installation and replacement costs, which will be added in the final ADP, so the figure is likely to change.

claims.claim: The three allocations in the draft ADP's Table B-1 total $5,438,000.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 ADP, Table B-1
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Table B-1 p.34. The sum checks (3,227,000 + 1,479,000 + 732,000 = 5,438,000), which rounds to the $5.45M headline budget.

claims.claim: The draft ADP says Congressional Directed Spending funds for EM installations and replacements are expected to run out by the end of 2026, so those costs are now in the 2027 budget.
claims.verbatim: The Congressional Directed Spending funds are expected to be expended by the end of 2026 and thus the costs of equipment installation and replacement are now included in the budget for 2027.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Appendix B p.26, with near-identical text on p.4. The ADP says these funds went to PSMFC 'Since 2023'. Soften to 'expected to'. The PCFMAC report calls them 'Community Directed Spending' and says they will be 'fully expended in 2027', which conflicts with the ADP. Follow the ADP. Note that trawl EM installation costs are NOT yet in the draft and come in the final ADP.

claims.claim: The Council's monitoring committee reported that fee revenue makes up $3.55 million of the estimated $5.45 million 2027 partial coverage budget.
claims.verbatim: The estimated 2027 budget is $5.45 million for partial coverage monitoring, with fee revenue comprising $3.55 million.
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, Partial Coverage Fishery Monitoring Advisory Committee Report
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, PCFMAC report p.3. Background (meeting September 15th, posted 09/23/2026). Slide 10's 'projected $3.55M' in observer fees corroborates it. Projected, so soften to 'an estimated'.

claims.claim: NMFS told the Council that as of October 1st, $3.19 million in observer fees had been assessed out of a projected $3.55 million.
claims.verbatim: Fee revenue is still being assessed for landings in 2026; as of October 1st, $3.19M in Observer Fees had been assessed out of the projected $3.55M
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 10. In window.

claims.claim: NMFS expects to monitor 2,742 trips and an estimated 16,374 days in the full coverage component in 2027.
claims.verbatim: In 2027, NMFS expects to monitor 2,742 trips, consisting of an estimated 16,374 days in the full coverage component of the program
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Executive Summary p.4. Table B-3 checks out (968 + 1,774 = 2,742 trips and 9,740 + 6,634 = 16,374 days). Projection, so write 'expects to'.

claims.claim: NMFS expects to monitor 1,404 trips and 4,408 days in the partial coverage component in 2027.
claims.verbatim: and 1,404 trips and 4,408 days in the partial coverage component.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Executive Summary p.4. Table B-3 checks out (316 + 194 + 894 = 1,404 trips and 1,290 + 973 + 2,145 = 4,408 days). Compared with 2026 (C38), partial coverage monitoring is planned 69 trips lower despite a larger budget. The documents give no single reason, so do not assert one. Preliminary.

claims.claim: For 2026, NMFS's final plan expected to monitor 4,341 trips and 22,110 days in total.
claims.verbatim: Overall, NMFS will implement 10 sampling strata in 2026 and expects to monitor 4,341 trips and 22,110 days,
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries, Information Bulletin 26-02
claims.notes: Fetched via WebFetch on 2026-10-15. BACKGROUND, outside the window (bulletin dated January 13th). The bulletin splits this into 2,868 trips and 17,461 days in full coverage, and the components sum correctly. Use it as the year-ago baseline only.

claims.claim: For 2026, the partial coverage component was expected to monitor 1,473 trips and 4,649 days.
claims.verbatim: and 1,473 trips and 4,649 days in the partial coverage component.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries, Information Bulletin 26-02
claims.notes: Fetched via WebFetch on 2026-10-15. BACKGROUND. The arithmetic checks (2,868 + 1,473 = 4,341 and 17,461 + 4,649 = 22,110). The 2026 figures come from a final plan and the 2027 figures from a draft, so label the comparison 'draft versus final'.

claims.claim: NMFS expects 99.96% of retained catch in Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands trawl fisheries to be monitored in 2027, counting full and partial coverage.
claims.verbatim: % of Retained Catch Monitored by FMP and Gear-type, Full & Partial Coverage Trawl Fixed-Gear BSAI 99.96 88.74
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 8 ('Expected Monitoring in the AK Federal Fisheries in 2027'). The PCFMAC report shows the table as an image only, so the slide is the sole text source. Projection, so write 'expected'.

claims.claim: NMFS expects 88.74% of retained catch in Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands fixed-gear fisheries to be monitored in 2027.
claims.verbatim: Trawl Fixed-Gear BSAI 99.96 88.74
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 8, full plus partial coverage table. Projection.

claims.claim: NMFS expects 86.42% of retained catch in Gulf of Alaska trawl fisheries to be monitored in 2027.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 8, first table (Full and Partial Coverage), Trawl column. The second table on the slide (partial coverage only) gives GOA trawl 82.19, so do not mix the two tables. Projection.

claims.claim: NMFS expects only 14.25% of retained catch in Gulf of Alaska fixed-gear fisheries to be monitored in 2027.
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 8, first table (Full and Partial Coverage), Fixed-Gear column. The partial-coverage-only table gives GOA fixed-gear 10.24. 'Only' is editorial but fair given the other three cells. Projection.

claims.claim: The preliminary 2027 observer selection rate for Gulf of Alaska fixed-gear trips is 9.31% of 1,868 expected trips, or 174 observed trips.
claims.verbatim: Fixed-gear GOA 9.31 1,868 174
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 22, At-sea Observer block. ADP Table 4 and Table B-3 corroborate it. The arithmetic checks (9.31% x 1,868 = 174). The 2026 final rate was 10% per IB 26-02. Preliminary, and final rates come in December.

claims.claim: The preliminary 2027 observer selection rate for Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands fixed-gear trips is 31.35%.
claims.verbatim: Fixed-gear BSAI 31.35 253 79
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 22. The rate applies to 253 expected trips, with 79 observed. ADP Table 4 corroborates it. Preliminary.

claims.claim: The preliminary 2027 EM selection rate for Gulf of Alaska fixed-gear trips is 15.24% of 1,010 expected trips, or 154 monitored trips.
claims.verbatim: EM Fixed-gear GOA 15.24 1,010 154
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 22. ADP Table 4 corroborates it. The arithmetic checks (15.24% x 1,010 = 154). Preliminary.

claims.claim: The preliminary 2027 EM selection rate for Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands fixed-gear trips is 42.99%.
claims.verbatim: EM Fixed-gear BSAI 42.99 92 40
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 22. The rate applies to 92 expected trips, with 40 monitored. Preliminary. The ADP's rounded summary table on p.8 shows '42', while Table 4 shows 42.99.

claims.claim: All 894 expected Gulf of Alaska pelagic trawl EM trips are to be monitored at a 100% rate in 2027.
claims.verbatim: EM Trawl GOA EM Trawl GOA 100.00 894 894
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 22. Per the ADP, the 100% means EM at sea for compliance plus shoreside salmon and halibut counts. Biological sampling covers only 33% of deliveries (an estimated 298).

claims.claim: An expected 1,427 trips in 2027 fall in the no-selection pool, which has a 0% chance of monitoring.
claims.verbatim: No-selection No-selection 0.00 1,427 0
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries Alaska Fisheries Science Center, Draft 2027 ADP presentation to the Council
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, slide 22. Per the ADP, the no-selection pool covers fixed-gear vessels under 40 ft LOA and jig gear. Expected trips are an estimate based on 13 August 2025 to 12 August 2026 effort.

claims.claim: More than 90% of Alaska's federal fisheries by tonnage are in the full coverage program, leaving under 10% in partial coverage.
claims.verbatim: More than 90% of Alaska’s federal fisheries (by tonnage) are within the full coverage program. Monitoring resources are allocated amongst the remaining <10% (by tonnage) of partial coverage fisheries
claims.source_outlet: North Pacific Fishery Management Council, Partial Coverage Fishery Monitoring Advisory Committee Report
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, PCFMAC report p.2. The verbatim keeps the source's typographic apostrophe. ADP Appendix B corroborates it: the partial coverage fleet 'accounts for approximately 10% of the landed tonnage in the federal fisheries off Alaska'. Background.

claims.claim: The North Pacific Observer Program is responsible for monitoring a fleet of nearly a thousand vessels.
claims.verbatim: The North Pacific Observer Program (Observer Program) is the largest observer program in the country and is responsible for monitoring a fleet of nearly a thousand vessels
claims.source_outlet: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS), Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan
claims.notes: Verified against the PDF text extracted by scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py. Location, ADP Executive Summary p.4, repeated on p.1. 'Largest observer program in the country' is NMFS's own characterization. If used, attribute it ('which NMFS calls the largest in the country').

claims.claim: That fleet fishes across an Alaska Exclusive Economic Zone of roughly 3.77 million square kilometers.
claims.verbatim: across the Alaska Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) area of roughly 3.77 M km2

killed.claim: Community Directed Spending funds of $2 million that supported EM over the past 3 to 4 years will be fully expended in 2027 (PCFMAC report).
killed.why: This contradicts the primary ADP on both the fund's name and the year. The ADP says 'Congressional Directed Spending' funds are 'expected to be expended by the end of 2026'. The $2 million figure appears only in the PCFMAC summary and can't be reconciled. C32 uses the ADP version.

killed.claim: The 2027 draft ADP sets an objective of a fixed-gear EM pool of up to 178 vessels.
killed.why: The 2027 draft contains no such objective. 178 is Appendix C's 'current count'. 'Up to 178 vessels' was the Council's June 2025 recommendation for the 2026 ADP, and the June 2026 motion says 'up to 181 vessels'. C52 and C53 replace it.

killed.claim: Applying the under-3-trips threshold raises the observer sample rate from 12.60% to 13.46% (slide 27).
killed.why: The slide is internally inconsistent: 12.60 + 0.83 = 13.43, and ADP Table C-2 prints 13.43. C21 uses 13.43%.

killed.claim: The $6,003 per-vessel EM equipment cost applies to 123 active vessels.
killed.why: The 123 count appears only on slide 17 and conflicts with the 133 active vessels in Appendix C. The documents can't reconcile the two denominators. The $6,003 figure itself survives as C24.

killed.claim: GVEA's alert system has four levels (Alaska's News Source).
killed.why: KUAC and the News-Miner both describe three levels, with Level 3 as imminent controlled outages. GVEA's own explainer was unreachable (bot check), so the conflict can't be settled.

killed.claim: Bradish said the generation situation 'is not going to be a quick fix' (quoted as a single verbatim line).
killed.why: The wording differs between outlets. KUAC has 'the generation situation that we're in is not a quick fix, unfortunately' and the News-Miner has 'The generation system we find ourselves in is not going to be a quick fix'. No single verbatim version can be published, so paraphrase with attribution or use C84.

killed.claim: Any GVEA claim sourced to GVEA's own release (gvea.com news release on Energy Emergency Alerts).
killed.why: The page returned only 'Please wait while your request is being verified', so it was not fetched. The runner-up rests on three independent news outlets, and no primary source was reachable.
